I read the manifest and the relevant classic and core TypeScript sources. Evidence comes from `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts`, `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/parse.ts`, `packages/zod/src/v4/core/schemas.ts`, and `packages/zod/src/v4/core/parse.ts`. My last retrieval (locating `$ZodString`'s core parse body) was rejected at the 18-request tool budget, so the core string-matching body itself is unread — see "Unresolved" at the end.

## 1. How the transformation is represented

`z.string().transform(fn)` does not attach a transform to the string. The method is `ZodType.prototype.transform`, declared at `classic/schemas.ts:131-133` to return `ZodPipe<this, ZodTransform<Awaited<NewOut>, core.output<this>>>`, and implemented at `245-246`:

```ts
transform(tx) { return pipe(this, transform(tx)); }
```

Two helper factories build the nodes. `transform()` at `classic/schemas.ts:2291-2297` constructs `new ZodTransform({ type: "transform", transform: fn })`. `pipe(in_, out)` at `2559-2566` constructs `new ZodPipe({ type: "pipe", in: in_, out: out })`. `ZodPipe`'s initializer (`2546-2553`) calls `core.$ZodPipe.init(inst, def)` then `ZodType.init`, and stores `inst.in`/`inst.out`. `ZodTransform`'s initializer (`2249-2289`) calls `core.$ZodTransform.init` + `ZodType.init` and overrides `inst._zod.parse`.

Core shapes: `$ZodTransformDef` is `{ type: "transform", transform: (input, payload) => MaybeAsync<unknown> }` (`core/schemas.ts:3824-3827`); `$ZodPipeDef` is `{ type: "pipe", in: A, out: B }` (`4401-4409`), with internals `$ZodTypeInternals<core.output<B>, core.input<A>>` (`4411-4419`) — i.e. the pipe presents the transform's output as its output and the string's input as its input. So one string-with-transform becomes a two-node graph: `Pipe(in: ZodString, out: ZodTransform)`.

## 2. Order: input parse first, then transform

`$ZodPipe`'s `inst._zod.parse` (`core/schemas.ts:4432-4446`) handles forward (decode) direction at `4441-4445`: it calls `def.in._zod.run(payload, ctx)` — the string — and passes the result to `handlePipeResult(left, def.out, ctx)` (the transform). Only the backward direction runs `out` first (`4433-4438`).

Within each node, `$ZodType`'s `run` runs the node's own `parse` and then its attached checks (`core/schemas.ts:297-320`), so the string's type check/refinements run before the pipe advances. `handlePipeResult` (`4449-4457`) then invokes `next._zod.run({ value: left.value, issues: left.issues }, ctx)` at `4456`, handing the parsed string to the transform. `$ZodTransform.parse` (`3844-3864`) then calls `def.transform(payload.value, payload)` (`3849`) and assigns `payload.value = _out` (`3862`), returning the payload. It never revalidates; it marks itself `optin = "optional"` (`3841`).

## 3. Which issues stop the pipe, and the exception

`handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4449-4457`) is the gate. Its comment at `4450` and code at `4451-4454`: if `left.issues.some((iss) => iss.code !== "unrecognized_keys")`, it sets `left.aborted = true` and returns `left` — the transform is never run. The single exception is the issue code **`unrecognized_keys`**, which describes extra input keys rather than the piped value, so the pipe continues. `aborted` is the payload's whole-pipe flag (`core/schemas.ts:47-48`). The classic transform also installs a `payload.addIssue` shim (`classic/schemas.ts:2262-2276`) for `ctx`-reported custom issues. An async transform under sync parsing throws `$ZodAsyncError` (`core/schemas.ts:3858-3859`, mirrored at `classic/schemas.ts:2279-2284`); encode/backward throws `$ZodEncodeError` (`3845-3847`, `2258-2260`).

## 4. How the transformed value is carried onward

The value travels by mutating the shared payload: `payload.value = _out` in core (`3862`) or `payload.value = output` in classic (`2285`), and the same payload object is returned (`3863`, `2286`). The pipe yields whatever `out._zod.run` returned (`4456`), so downstream nodes read the transformed value from `payload.value`. Terminally, core `_parse` (`core/parse.ts:22-37`) builds `{ async: false }`, calls `schema._zod.run`, rejects a Promise, throws on `result.issues.length`, and returns `result.value` (`34`); `_safeParse` (`71-79`) returns `{ success: true, data: result.value }` (`78`). Classic `parse`/`safeParse` are thin aliases: `core._parse(ZodRealError)` and `core._safeParse(ZodRealError)` (`classic/parse.ts:8-27`).

## Unresolved

I did not read core `$ZodString`'s `parse` body (hence the exact string issue code emitted, e.g. `invalid_type`), the classic `ZodType` prototype `parse`/`safeParse` method definitions, or `util.aborted`'s implementation. Conclusions about ordering rest on `$ZodPipe`/`handlePipeResult` wiring and `$ZodType.run`, not on the string's own body.
